label: override_express
point: Held the FTDA requires proof of actual dilution, not likelihood of dilution, reinforcing that reading with the 1127 definition of dilution as an actual 'lessening of the capacity' of a mark.
change: Struck the 1127 definition of 'dilution' (the Act moved to a likelihood-of-dilution standard with blurring/tarnishment definitions in 1125(c)).
why: The Act removed the definitional text the Court used to confirm the actual-dilution requirement and replaced the standard with likelihood of dilution; the House report discusses Moseley's actual-dilution holding as the problem addressed.

label: override_express
point: Held that 'use' of a firearm under 924(c)(1) requires active employment, so mere proximity and accessibility of a gun to drugs is not enough.
change: Restructured 924(c)(1) and added liability for anyone who 'in furtherance of any such crime, possesses a firearm', plus tiered minimums.
why: The new possession-in-furtherance prong reaches the passive possession Bailey held outside 'use'; the committee report describes Bailey's active-employment holding as the reason for the change.

label: unrelated
point: Held an employer need not justify applying a federal DOT vision standard just because the standard could be waived; it cited 12101 only as 'et seq.' for the ADA.
change: Rewrote the 12101 findings (dropped the 43,000,000 figure and the 'discrete and insular minority' finding).
why: The decision did not rely on the findings; the rewritten findings have no bearing on its safety-regulation holding.

label: override_express
point: Held that 1001 ('any department or agency of the United States') does not reach false statements made in judicial proceedings.
change: Rewrote 1001 to cover matters within the jurisdiction of the 'executive, legislative, or judicial branch' of the Government.
why: The new words reach the judicial branch, reversing the decision's point, and the report says the bill responds to Hubbard.

label: related
point: Held ADEA backpay and liquidated damages are not excludable under 104(a)(2) as damages received on account of personal injuries.
change: Added that emotional distress is not treated as physical injury or sickness under 104(a)(2) (along with limiting the exclusion to physical injuries).
why: The amendment narrows the exclusion further, in the same direction as Schleier, so it would not change the result; the report mentions Schleier as background, not as a decision to reverse.

label: related
point: Held a third party who paid another's tax under protest to discharge a lien may sue for a refund under 28 U.S.C. 1346(a)(1), noting the 7426 levy remedy was unavailable to her.
change: Added 7426(a)(4), a civil action to contest the valuation after a certificate of discharge is issued under new 6325(b)(4) substitution of value.
why: The law adds a new pre-payment remedy for third parties in Williams' position but does not take away the refund-suit route the Court recognized; the report names Williams as background.

label: codifies
point: Held that 506(a) requires the replacement-value standard, not foreclosure value, for collateral a Chapter 13 debtor keeps under cram-down.
change: Added 506(a)(2): in Chapter 7 or 13 cases for individuals, personal property is valued at replacement value without deduction for costs of sale, and household goods at retail price.
why: The amendment writes the replacement-value rule into the statute and fills in details Rash left open; it agrees with the holding.

label: unrelated
point: Section 1221 was cited only in passing in the dissent (citing Gillette Motor Transport); the case decided whether S-corporation discharge-of-indebtedness income increases shareholder basis under 108.
change: Corrected a parenthesis in the 1221 commodities derivative definition.
why: The 1221 change is a technical punctuation fix unrelated to the decision; the report names Gitlitz for a change made elsewhere (108), not in 1221.

label: override_implicit
point: Held the FDA lacked authority under the FDCA to regulate tobacco products, reasoning in part that under 331(a) misbranded tobacco 'devices' would have to be removed from the market.
change: Inserted 'tobacco product' into 331(a)'s prohibited acts, as part of giving FDA express authority over tobacco products under a new chapter.
why: Congress gave FDA the jurisdiction over tobacco that the Court found missing, so the decision's conclusion no longer holds; the packet shows no passage naming the case.

label: override_express
point: Held a patent-law counterclaim does not make a case 'arise under' patent law for 1338(a), so the Federal Circuit lacked appellate jurisdiction under 1295(a)(1).
change: Replaced the state-court exclusivity sentence in 1338(a) with a bar on any State court jurisdiction over any claim for relief arising under patent, plant variety or copyright law (with related changes to 1295 for compulsory counterclaims).
why: The law makes patent counterclaims (any claim for relief) exclusively federal and, through the related 1295 change, gives the Federal Circuit the appeals Holmes denied; the report names Holmes as the decision addressed.

label: override_express
point: Held that when a non-filer receives a notice of deficiency before filing a return, the 2-year look-back in 6512(b)(3)(B) applies, so the Tax Court cannot refund withheld taxes.
change: Added that when the notice is mailed in the third year after the due date and no return was filed, the look-back period is 3 years.
why: The new sentence gives taxpayers in Lundy's situation a 3-year look-back, reversing the result, and the report describes Lundy as the case addressed.
